szlak-papieski.header: Papal Trail – Sightseeing Tour of Zakopane and Surroundings
szlak-papieski.header2: In the Footsteps of Saint John Paul II and Zakopane’s History
szlak-papieski.text: Join us for a unique, peaceful sightseeing tour that combines spirituality, history, and Highlander culture. The “Papal Trail” is ideal for those who want to discover Zakopane and its surroundings without strenuous hikes. For 4–5 hours, we travel by comfortable minibus with a guide, visiting the most important and touching places associated with Saint John Paul II and the region’s history.

list.1: We start our journey at Toporowa Cyrhla, where the Papal Stone is located – the symbolic beginning of the Papal Trail. With a stunning view of the Tatra Mountains, Giewont, and Kasprowy Wierch, you can already feel the special atmosphere of this trip.
list.2: Next, we head to the Chapel in Jaszczurówka – a gem of Zakopane architecture designed by Stanisław Witkiewicz. Inside, we take a quiet moment to feel the spirit of Highland faith.
list.3: We drive through areas dear to Karol Wojtyła’s heart: Olczyska Valley and the base of Nosal. We also admire Wielka Krokiew and the ski jump complex – symbols of Zakopane’s sporting spirit.
list.4: Wielka Krokiew and the ski jump complex – we admire the famous ski jump and its smaller counterparts from the outside.
list.5: Next, we pass streets named after prominent Zakopane cultural figures and arrive at Kościeliska Street and the cemetery at Pęksowy Brzyzek. This is the oldest part of the city, featuring the wooden Gąsienica Chapel and the “U Jana Wnuka” inn.
list.6: In the second part of the trip, we stop by Villa Koliba – one of the most important examples of the Zakopane style. Then we visit the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Fatima in Krzeptówki. It houses Poland’s largest wooden altar and the papal altar from the Holy Mass celebrated by John Paul II in 1997 under Wielka Krokiew.
list.7: On the way back, we visit a traditional shepherd’s hut in Witów where you can buy original oscypek cheese and taste fresh bundz. We also stop in Chochołów – a unique village of over 30 original wooden houses, known as a “living open-air museum.”
list.8: We’ll also visit the workshop of famous sculptor Jan Ziędera, who gladly shares his passion and works with visitors. The trip ends with a ride over the top of Gubałówka – from here you can see the whole of Zakopane and the majestic Tatra Mountains. The perfect end to a day full of reflection, beautiful views, and unique encounters with the history and spirit of Podhale. The Papal Trail is not just a bus tour – it's a journey into the heart of culture, memory, and tradition.

tatry-i-zakopane.text: Join us for an unforgettable adventure in the heart of the Tatras! Our mountain trips are the perfect way to explore majestic peaks, picturesque valleys, and crystal-clear lakes. From walks around Morskie Oko, hikes to Kasprowy Wierch, to relaxing in the Chochołowska Valley – there’s something for everyone. We offer both easy trails for families and challenges for adrenaline enthusiasts, including an exciting trip to the Slovak Paradise. Join us, explore Zakopane with a guide, and feel the magic of Tatra nature!

list.1: Kasprowy Wierch - Kasprowy Wierch (1987 m above sea level) is one of the most popular Tatra peaks. You can reach it by cable car from Kuźnice or hike up. The easiest trail is the green one from Kuźnice via Myślenickie Turnie (7 km, approx. 3.5h). Alternatively, the blue trail through Hala Gąsienicowa offers stunning views. From the summit, you can enjoy a panorama of the Western Tatras, High Tatras, and the Slovak Silent Valley. At the top, there is a High-Altitude Meteorological Observatory and a restaurant.
list.2: Morskie Oko - The largest lake in the Tatras, located at 1395 m above sea level. The trail from Palenica Białczańska (red trail, 9 km) takes about 2.5h one way. Along the way, you pass the Mickiewicz Waterfalls. The trail is easy, ideal for families, though it can be crowded in season. At the lake, there is a PTTK shelter where you can rest and try local delicacies.
list.3: Strążyska Valley - An ideal trail for beginners and families with children. The red trail (4 km round trip, approx. 1.5h) leads to the Siklawica Waterfall (23 m). Along the way, you pass Strążyska Glade with a buffet. The valley offers a beautiful view of Giewont. The trail is easy, partially gravel, and suitable for strollers.
list.4: Kościeliska Valley - One of the most beautiful Tatra valleys. The green trail from Kiry to the Ornak Shelter (5.5 km, approx. 1.5h) is easy and offers views of limestone rock formations and caves (e.g., Mroźna Cave, additional fee). In spring, the valley is adorned with crocuses. The trail is wide, perfect for family walks.
list.5: Chochołowska Valley - The largest valley in the Tatras, famous for crocuses and pastoral huts. The green trail from Siwa Polana to the PTTK Shelter (7.5 km, approx. 2h) is easy, partially paved, suitable for strollers and bikes. The valley features a chapel from the movie 'Janosik' and a plaque commemorating John Paul II’s visit.
list.6: Guided sightseeing tour of Zakopane - the Papal Trail. Route suitable for groups of all ages, with a professional guide.

more.header2: Legends and Secrets of the Dunajec Gorge!
more.text: Was it the knight Ferkowicz chasing the king of snakes, or did Bolesław Chrobry carve the river's outlet? Discover the legends and secrets of the Dunajec Gorge!

1.text: The Dunajec Gorge is one of the most beautiful river gorges in Europe. It was formed millions of years ago when the river cut through the limestone rocks of the Pieniny.

2.text: Dunajec rafting has been organized for over 200 years! Initially, raftsmen transported goods, and since the 19th century, they have been taking tourists, including aristocrats.

3.text: The rafting route is about 12 km long and passes through seven scenic bends. The most famous is the one around Trzy Korony, the highest peak in the Pieniny.

4.text: The Pieniny are home to lynxes, wolves, and fire salamanders. Lucky visitors might spot a golden eagle circling above the gorge.

5.text: Highlanders believe that the outlaw Janosik hid in the caves of the Dunajec. The rocks called 'Janosik’s Gate' are said to be his secret escape route.

6.text: The rock formations in the gorge have their own names, like 'White Lady' or 'Falcon’s Path.' Each hides a story told by the raftsmen.

7.text: The Dunajec Gorge inspired Sienkiewicz’s 'The Deluge' and has appeared in Polish films, captivating artists for centuries.

8.text: Raftsmen are masters of storytelling! Their humorous tales, passed down through generations, make the rafting a real show.

9.header: Dunajec – A River of Two Countries
9.text: The Dunajec marks the border between Poland and Slovakia. Raftsmen joke that rafting is the easiest 'international trip.'

10.text: Rafting takes place from April to October. Spring offers blooming nature, while autumn dazzles with the colors of the Pieniny.

spacer-w-koronach-drzew.text: The Treetop Walk Bachledka is located in the heart of a species-diverse forest in Pieniny National Park. It shows visitors why the nature of Spišská Magura is unique. Together with us, you will explore the local forests, become part of forest life, and learn about various rare animal and plant species. Early morning departure from Zakopane towards Bachledova Valley. Here, we invite you to take the gondola lift (approx. 7-minute ride), which will take you to the summit of Spišská Magura.

list.1: While walking along the path, you can use many informational boards placed at several stops along the horizontal section of the path. The boards contain interesting information about the local fauna, flora, forest life, conservation, and the destructive power of weather.
list.2: The over 600-meter-long route will take visitors through a species-diverse forest with many surprises and curiosities.

tripprogram.text: After the tour, we return by gondola to the parking lot, from where we head through the High Tatras (Tatranská Lomnica, Starý Smokovec) to Štrbské Pleso. Here, we invite you for free time. For those interested, a walk around the lake takes about 40 minutes. Štrbské Pleso—or Szczyrbskie Jezioro in Polish—is located at an altitude of 1346 m above sea level. Often compared to our Morskie Oko, the lake is surrounded by spruce forests, heavily damaged by a hurricane in 2004. This settlement has the status of a climatic health resort and is also a well-known ski resort. This beautiful place almost disappeared in the mid-19th century when locals wanted to drain it and turn it into pasture. After a walk around the picturesque lake, return to Zakopane. The over 600-meter-long route will take visitors through a species-diverse forest with many surprises and curiosities.

jaskinia-bielanska.text: Bielańska Cave is the only cave in the Slovak Tatras open to visitors. It was the first cave in Europe illuminated with electric light. To reach the entrance at 890 m above sea level, you must climb 122 meters in elevation, covering a 1370-meter-long route, with the tour lasting 70 minutes. In the first half of the 18th century, the cave entrances were known to gold seekers but remained secret for a long time. The entrance was rediscovered by L. Gulden and gold seeker Fabry in 1826. In 1896, a power plant on the Biała River supplied electricity to the cave, which could only be visited three times a day. The guide opened it even if only one tourist was waiting. Today, the cave features numerous dripstone waterfalls, pagoda-like stalagmites, and small lakes. Later, we drive under the Tatra Mountains to Štrbské Pleso, a lake on the Slovak side, just a 5-minute walk from the parking lot where your driver will be waiting. Passing through Starý Smokovec and Tatranská Lomnica (a ski resort complex), you will see the beauty and power of nature, as the area was devastated by a massive hurricane in 2004, which felled 14,000 hectares of forests.

list.1: Štrbské Pleso - 300 years ago, there were three water reservoirs where the current lake is. The lake basin was formed by the melting of dead ice about 80 m thick left by a retreating glacier. Research in 1998 confirmed suspicions that the lake was formed by a massive earthquake that sealed the moraine and suddenly raised the water level, as mentioned in historical sources—the chronicler Gašpar Hain of Levoča mentions the formation of a new, large lake after an earthquake in the Tatras on August 6, 1662. The surface area of Štrbské Pleso is 19.76 ha. The maximum depth is 20 m, with a volume of 1,284,000 m³. The lake is covered with ice for an average of 155 days a year. It has no inflowing or outflowing rivers.
list.2: Starý Smokovec - A popular tourist center, mainly for skiers and hiking enthusiasts. It is also an important hub for the electrified narrow-gauge railway connecting Poprad, Tatranská Lomnica, and Štrbské Pleso. Starý Smokovec also has the lower station of the funicular to Smokovecké Sedlo. A very famous building in Starý Smokovec is the Grand Hotel, built in 1904. Starý Smokovec is home to the headquarters of the Mountain Rescue Service (HZS). The forests around Smokovec were almost completely destroyed by a hurricane on November 19, 2004. The wind felled trees over at least 14,000 hectares, destroying about 60% of the spruce population in the Slovak High Tatras. About 3 million m³ of wood lay on the southern slopes of the Tatras. Clearing the fallen forest took about 2 years, while regeneration will take about 100 years. A monument commemorating the event was built in Starý Smokovec, revealing a view of the Tatras and Poprad. This was not the end of the disaster, as a few years later—in April 2013—a fire burned 22 hectares of young forest.
list.3: Tatranská Lomnica - The settlement was established around 1881 and was initially treated as a tourist destination. In 1893, the first hotel—Lomnica—was built here. A significant increase in tourist importance dates back to the late 1930s when the construction of an extremely modern cable car to Lomnica with an intermediate station above Lomnický Pond was completed. The final section of the cable car overcomes a height difference of 850 meters on one span, with the cabin about 300 meters above the ground. Since 2001, the lower section has been closed due to unprofitability and the need for renovation. It is unknown if it will ever reopen; perhaps a museum will be established in the lower station building, designed by the famous Slovak architect Dušan Jurkovič.

wieliczka.text: The Wieliczka Salt Mine is considered one of the seven wonders of Poland. Exploring the beautiful underground chambers, peeking into amazing salt lakes, admiring unique carpentry structures, and one-of-a-kind salt sculptures, you will feel the unique atmosphere. In 2004, it turned out that the brine located 104 meters underground is a fantastic place for windsurfing. Mateusz Kusznierewicz himself tried it, supported by a huge blower and a crowd of enthusiastic fans. A nearly 3-kilometer walk along a winding route with 800 steps to climb will take you 135 meters underground, offering not only an unforgettable adventure but also a 'salt dose' of health!

wieden.text: Located on the Danube, the capital of Austria attracts with its rich history, culture, and traditions. The historic city center, full of monuments from all historical periods, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2001. Due to its wealth of attractions, Vienna is one of the most visited cities in Europe. At the end of the 18th century, the most famous composers of the time worked here, hence the term Viennese Classics, collectively referring to Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and Ludwig van Beethoven.

list.header: During the trip to Vienna, many attractions await us:
list.1: Center - The Ring is one of the most recognizable streets in Vienna. It is home to the most important landmarks of the Austrian capital. The Ring, like a ring, surrounds the entire historic center. The avenue was built on the site of the old city walls, demolished in the 19th century. Although the purpose of the Ringstrasse was to prevent rebellion against the authorities, it turned out to be an elegant boulevard fully dedicated to the residents of Vienna. The most beautiful palaces and many public buildings were built here. One of the first attractions you will see after driving along the Ring is the Hundertwasser House—an unusual tenement house distinguished by interesting colors and irregular shapes, built by the famous architect of the same name. After admiring this interesting work of contemporary architecture, we will explore the city with a guide. Here, you will have the opportunity to visit and hear interesting facts about the representative Charles Square, the Hofburg, considered the most important historic building in Vienna. This was the former residence of the Habsburgs, about 700 years old. The building is impressive, covering over 240,000 m². It has 19 courtyards, 50 staircases, 2,600 rooms, museums, chapels, gardens, libraries, and other rooms. Other attractions in the center of the Austrian capital include Kohlmarkt, Graben, and St. Stephen's Cathedral.
list.2: Belvedere - The greatest treasure of Vienna and one of the most beautiful Baroque buildings in the world. It was created for Prince Eugene of Savoy in the first half of the 18th century. The complex consists of two palaces and a garden. The Lower and Upper Belvedere are the works of architect Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt. The garden, created by Dominique Girard, features a French style with various statues, including sphinxes, fountains, and countless plants.
list.3: Schönbrunn Palace and Gardens - The summer residence of Empress Sisi is the most popular attraction in the city. Called the Vienna Versailles, it impresses with its representative building, inspired by the residence of Louis XIV. It served members of the Habsburg dynasty and their distinguished guests. Today, open to visitors, it is one of the most important Austrian monuments—inscribed on the UNESCO World Cultural and Natural Heritage List. It is characterized by exceptional richness of architectural decorations, wall paintings, gilding, and beautiful mosaic floors. The palace also includes a zoo and a palm house. Schönbrunn also features a French-style park complex with a boxwood maze.

budapeszt.text: Budapest is undoubtedly one of the most interesting and beautiful cities in Europe. Its charming location on the Danube, the wonderful hills of Buda full of geothermal springs, interesting history, and rich architecture attract crowds of tourists from all over the world to the capital of our Hungarian brothers every year.

list.header: During the trip to Budapest, many attractions await us:
list.1: Heroes' Square - Located at the end of the famous Andrássy Avenue, the square has been adorned since 1929 with the monumental Millennium Monument, symbolizing over a thousand years of Hungarian state history.
list.2: Vajdahunyad Castle - Built at the turn of the 19th and 20th centuries, Vajdahunyad Castle, like the Millennium Monument, was a symbol of the thousand years of Hungary. The building is characterized by great architectural diversity, as the author intended to combine twenty stylistically diverse castles, palaces, and churches into a coherent whole. The intention succeeded brilliantly, and today the castle is a must-see on any Budapest tour.
list.3: Gellért Hill - The best viewpoint in Budapest owes its name to St. Gerard (Gellért), who allegedly ended his life here as a martyr in the mid-11th century. The massive hill is built with remnants of an Austrian fortress erected in 1850, crowned by a 40-meter Freedom Monument built after World War II. The entire site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
list.4: Castle Hill - This is the oldest and most attractive part of Budapest. For centuries, it was the seat of Hungarian rulers, who spared no expense to show their wealth. The historic character of the city is most emphasized by the Royal Castle, whose origins date back to the 13th century, and the famous Matthias Church—one of the most beautiful temples in Hungary. Tourists are delighted not only by the monumental buildings but also by the streets of the Buda Old Town, full of charm and mystery.
list.5: St. Stephen's Basilica - One of the most important Hungarian temples impresses not only with its power but also with its craftsmanship. A curiosity of the temple is the right hand of St. Stephen—the patron of the temple and the first king of Hungary.
list.6: Parliament - The undisputed symbol of Budapest was built at the turn of the 19th and 20th centuries. This neo-Gothic gem is still the seat of the Hungarian government, and the Hungarian coronation jewels are also stored here. The massive dimensions of the building (268 m x 123 m) make it not only one of the most beautiful but also one of the largest national parliament buildings in the world.
list.7: Danube Cruise - At the end of the tour, you will have the opportunity to see the most attractive places in Budapest from the perspective of a ship. The cruise will be the perfect end to this exciting day.

dookola-tatr.text: Orava Castle Built in the 13th century on a massive 112-meter-high rock, Orava Castle is the most originally located object in Slovakia. Rebuilt and expanded over several hundred years, today it is an excellent example of various techniques of defensive architecture. The castle was originally the seat of the owners of Orava. In 1868, the first museum exhibition on Slovak lands was created here. The castle serves museum functions to this day. During the tour, you will see historical, archaeological, and ethnographic exhibitions. The highlight of the walk through the museum will be entering the highest castle chambers. Demänovská Cave of Liberty - The attractiveness of Demänovská Cave of Liberty is evidenced by the fact that it is the most visited cave in Slovakia. Multicolored dripstone formations of various shapes, tufa lakes, and an underground river make this object one of the most beautiful caves in Europe.

rafting-po-dunajcu.info: The rafting season runs from April 1 to October 31—Thursday, Friday, and Sunday. So, we invite you on the trip every day! NOTE: Bring a change of clothes. Rafting is allowed in sandals, waterproof shoes, or barefoot. No high heels.
rafting-po-dunajcu.text: Extreme rafting on the Dunajec River is an unforgettable adventure for those craving adrenaline and a close connection with nature. The gorge offers strong currents, rocky sections, and spectacular views of steep cliffs that intensify the thrill. The rafting route can vary depending on water levels and weather conditions, making each trip unique. Fully equipped and under the supervision of experienced instructors, participants can safely face the power of nature. This activity combines sport, challenge, and fun, turning every moment on the water into an unforgettable experience. It’s the perfect option for active people who want to experience wild nature in safe conditions.

list.header: Rafting as the perfect team-building adventure. Extreme rafting on the Dunajec River is an excellent option for organized groups, companies, or families seeking excitement and bonding in a unique setting. The rafting trip is combined with free time at the Niedzica Dam and the wooden church in Dębno, extending the adventure and allowing for relaxation after the intense experience. The organizers provide full logistical support and professional lifeguard supervision. This activity not only offers unforgettable thrills but also strengthens connections among participants and leaves lasting memories.
list.1: Boat cruise on Lake Czorsztyn: During the cruise, you can admire the dam, the ruins of Czorsztyn Castle, Niedzica Castle, the Czorsztyn Open-Air Museum, and the beautiful mountain landscape. Such a cruise is an adventure that will stay in your memory for a long time!
list.2: Niedzica Castle: It is here in the castle dungeons that you can see the torture chamber with stocks, where, according to legend, Janosik was shackled.
list.3: Tour of the Dunajec Dam The main Czorsztyn-Niedzica Dam is the largest earth dam in Poland, 56 m high and 404 m long.
list.4: The Miniature Park of Podhale, Orava, and Spiš is an absolutely unique place. In one place, you can admire the most beautiful sacral monuments, castles, and much more.
list.5: During the trip, you will also see the historic wooden church in Dębno from the 15th century, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site—it was here that Janosik married Maryna...
